name: Khurem Farooq
current_role: CEO & board member, Verdiva Bio (oral obesity/cardiometabolic biotech, London & San Francisco)
profile: British biotech executive with 20+ years in drug development and commercialization, previously SVP of Genentech's immunology and ophthalmology unit. He was CEO of Gyroscope Therapeutics (acquired by Novartis, 2021) and co-founder/CEO of Aiolos Bio (acquired by GSK, 2024), and now leads Verdiva Bio, which is developing once-weekly oral GLP-1 and amylin therapies for obesity.
interesting_fact: Verdiva's lead program VRB-101 is an oral once-weekly GLP-1 (ecnoglutide) in Phase 2; the company was named a Fierce Biotech 'Fierce 15' winner in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in sales and marketing at Aventis, and holds a Biological Sciences degree from the University of Wolverhampton and an MBA from Aston University.

public_contacts.value: FTI Consulting (Ben Atwell, Michael Trace): ftiverdivacomms@fticonsulting.com

notes: Serial founder-CEO team: he and CSO Jane Hughes worked together at Gyroscope, Aiolos and now Verdiva. Earlier releases list Vigo Consulting as media agency (VerdivaBio@VigoConsulting.com); the latest (2026) lists FTI.

name: Dylan Kerler
profile: English entrepreneur in his twenties and one of Pump.fun's three co-founders with Noah Tweedale and Alon Cohen. Pump.fun launched in January 2024, reportedly earned more than $350M in revenue in its first year from a 1% trading fee, and raised about $1.3B in its July 2025 PUMP token sale.
interesting_fact: The founders began as memecoin traders and built Pump.fun after repeatedly being victims of rug pulls, aiming for a launch platform where everyone is on the same playing field.
notes: Extremely low profile: WIRED reports Kerler 'has little public association with Pump.Fun' and his name surfaced only via corporate filings. No published contact or verified social account found. Platform faces regulatory/legal scrutiny (UK FCA warning, US lawsuit).

name: Victor Lugger
current_role: Co-founder, sunday (restaurant QR-payment app); co-founder & co-CEO, Big Mamma Group
profile: French entrepreneur (born 1984, Strasbourg; HEC Paris) and former CFO of crowdfunding platform My Major Company. With HEC classmate Tigrane Seydoux he founded Italian restaurant group Big Mamma in 2015 (24 restaurants in five countries by 2023; majority sold to McWin in 2023), and in 2021 co-founded sunday with Christine de Wendel, raising $100M; sunday now serves 5,000+ restaurants.
interesting_fact: He and Seydoux were named Gault & Millau Entrepreneurs of the Year in 2017 and co-wrote the cookbook 'Big Mamma: Cuisine italienne, con molto amore' (Marabout, 2016).
deep_cut_fact: Before Big Mamma, he and Seydoux first set out to build a chain of creperies, then pivoted to Italian food, which they judged more universal; they reconnected via investor Stephane Courbit.
notes: Exact current title at sunday not confirmed on the official site (co-founded with Christine de Wendel). Big Mamma backers included Xavier Niel and Stephane Courbit.

name: Bu Xiangwei
current_role: Listed as a representative figure / co-founder of Orienspace (东方空间), Chinese commercial launch company; exact title not confirmed
profile: Bu Xiangwei (布向伟) is named alongside Shi Shengqing as a key figure of Orienspace, founded June 2020 and headquartered in Haiyang/Yantai, Shandong, with R&D in Beijing; Yao Song (ex-DeePhi Tech founder) is CEO. Orienspace builds the Gravity rocket series and is valued ~$1B.
interesting_fact: Orienspace's Gravity-1, launched from a sea platform in January 2024, is the world's most powerful all-solid-fuel carrier rocket (about 6.5 t to LEO) and had four successful launches through September 2026.
notes: Linked to Orienspace only via Chinese Wikipedia (https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/东方空间), which names him as a representative figure without title or background; personal biography could not be verified (web-search quota exhausted, Baidu blocked). Chinese-language outreach via pr@ advisable.
